question: Do crater interiors show the same sign of orbital magnetic contrast, and how sensitive is it to altitude, reference area and mapped surface geology?

sites.caution: Large catalog window in the Ladon region. The revised catalog flags this entry Misidentified. It is retained transparently as a regional window, excluded from primary crater conclusions, and is not a validated rim or an independent control.

matching: Exact USGS SIM3292 map unit; outside means reweighted to inside unit area on common support. Report support fraction; never treat a map unit as deep lithology or exact age.
uncertainty: Sensitivity envelopes are not confidence intervals. No independent pixel counts, p-values or origin probabilities.

prediction_rules.statement: All primary crater interiors have smaller mean orbital |B| than their nearby reference rings.
prediction_rules.criterion: Each baseline ratio < 1; robustness checked across all predefined geometry and altitude variants.
prediction_rules.scope: Restrictive observable rule only; failure cannot reject thermal or chemical alteration.

prediction_rules.statement: All primary crater interiors have larger mean orbital |B| than their nearby reference rings.
prediction_rules.criterion: Each baseline ratio > 1; same sensitivity checks.
prediction_rules.scope: Restrictive observable rule only; failure cannot reject remanence acquisition or a past dynamo.
